rationale: A wins because it keeps the story on the facts and turns weak spots into reporter questions instead of pretending they are conclusions. Its angle, "Rivian's next revenue line is selling electricity to everyone else's EVs," gives a markets reporter a clean P&L story and names the proof needed before anyone opens their mouth. B has real material, but "Rivian just bet that an exclusive charging network isn't worth keeping" smuggles in a moat thesis the update never supplied; clever is not the same as sourced.
gaps_in_A: "Rivian adds Tesla-style plugs and opens its network with no automaker partner in sight" slightly upgrades "no partnership announced" into a stronger absence claim. Keep the distinction clean.
"whether 'improves utilization' is a polite way of saying stalls sit empty" is sharp, but it cannot become copy without utilization data.
The infrastructure angle bundles connector standards, open access, app-only access, and no partnership into one lane. A pure CCS/NACS rollout angle might be cleaner for a standards reporter.
gaps_in_B: "Rivian just bet that an exclusive charging network isn't worth keeping" asserts motive and strategic conclusion the update does not prove.
"The prevailing belief: a proprietary fast-charging network is a moat" imports an industry premise without evidence from the supplied facts.
"with no automaker partnership to force its hand" turns "no partnership announced" into a causal claim. That is a fact-check trap.
"what it says about the moat thesis the rest of the industry still holds" is a broad industry claim with no support in the update. The angle needs sourcing or it needs to be demoted to a question.
